# transformer-twin-lab

> Interactive browser demos on digital twins of power transformers, built for a conference talk in the context of CIGRE JWG A2/D2.65. Every demo runs entirely client-side: no build step, no CDN, no web fonts, no external requests, nothing uploaded. The recurring theme is honest uncertainty: where a diagnosis actually sits, how wide the interval around it really is, and what a measurement does and does not tell you.

All pages are bilingual English/German (switch with `?lang=en` / `?lang=de`, default English) and have a light/dark theme switch. Everything is derived from public standards and CIGRE technical brochures, cited on the landing page; there are no device-specific parameter sets anywhere. The pages work offline from a local disk, which is deliberate: they are shown live on conference beamers over unreliable WLAN.

Author: Alexander Alber. A personal project in a CIGRE JWG A2/D2.65 context, not a product and not affiliated with any employer. Copyright (c) 2026, all rights reserved; there is deliberately no open-source licence yet, so the code is not offered for reuse. Vendored libraries under `docs/assets/` keep their own licences.

## Demos

- [Duval triangle under uncertainty](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/duval.html): One DGA result placed in Duval Triangle 1, with the fault zones after IEC 60599 and CIGRE TB 771, and the cloud of diagnoses that the same measurement could equally have meant. A slider sets the relative measurement uncertainty from 5% to 35% and a Monte Carlo cloud of possible true points is drawn, each point coloured by the zone it lands in, with the resulting distribution over diagnoses given as percentages. The point at which the diagnosis starts crossing zone boundaries is around ±15%, which is inside the range of an ordinary laboratory. A second control switches the error geometry between plain euclidean scatter and log-ratio (compositional) geometry, which is the appropriate geometry for data that are constrained to sum to 100%, and the two produce visibly different clouds from the same error bar. The example goes back to an idea by Tony McGrail.
- [Duval pentagon under uncertainty](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/pentagon.html): The same question asked in five gases instead of three. One point in Duval Pentagon 1 and 2 (Duval and Lamarre 2014, CIGRE TB 771), and the region of diagnoses that the laboratory error bar really covers. Because the pentagon maps five concentrations into two dimensions, the propagated uncertainty is not a simple disc, and the demo shows the resulting spread of fault classifications rather than a single verdict.
- [Thermal mini-twin](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/thermal.html): A year of top-oil and hot-spot temperature computed from a load profile with the IEC 60076-7 ONAN loading-guide equations (Heun integrator, low-pass ambient, Parton-Logan daily temperature cycle, a compressed 20-day year), and four different ways to propagate the uncertainty in it into the remaining life of the insulation. Ageing is DP-based after Ekenstam with a moisture-dependent rate constant (Emsley values as reported in Lundgaard et al. 2004). The four propagation methods are linearisation, the unscented transform, an unscented transform with a skew fit (shifted lognormal) and plain Monte Carlo, shown side by side so the differences between them are the point rather than a footnote. Four tabs: configuration, a live causal strip chart with a confidence band and events, remaining-life distributions, and a prose description of the model with its sources.
- [Moisture mini-twin](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/moisture.html): Where the water in a transformer actually sits. Moisture in paper is solved on a grid of 16 radial by 6 axial cells (copper out to oil, over the tank height) with implicit time stepping, a Robin boundary at the oil side and zero flux at the copper, diffusion after Foss and Guidi/Fullerton, solubility over temperature and a paper isotherm in relative saturation. The oil is a well-mixed reservoir in ppm while the oil temperature is stratified. Three things it is built to show: the same ppm reading means roughly five times the paper moisture at 20 C than at 80 C; an oil drying campaign removes only a few percent of the water and the oil reading is back within a day, and after a long treatment ends up higher than it started; and the cooling stage flattens the axial moisture spread. Manual ONAN/ONAF/OFAF switching after IEC 60076-7 Table 4. Sources include CIGRE TB 349, Guidi and Fullerton 1974 and Garcia et al. 2005.
- [Five levels of a digital twin](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/levels.html): One transformer and one thermal model taken through five capability levels, so that "digital twin" stops being a single word: describe the current state, diagnose a cooling fault, forecast the next 48 hours, choose between dispatch options, and close the loop. The five tabs are descriptive (what is happening), diagnostic (why), predictive (what happens next), prescriptive (what to do about it) and autonomous (doing it), all running on the same underlying simulation rather than on five different toy examples; the autonomous level is compared against the same plant run without the predictive logic.

## About the pages

- [Landing page](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/): All five demos with descriptions, plus the full source list (IEC 60599, IEC 60076-7, IEC 60076-2, CIGRE TB 771, TB 738, TB 349, Duval and Lamarre 2014, Lundgaard et al. 2004, Parton and Logan 1981, Guidi and Fullerton 1974, Garcia et al. 2005).
- [Repository](https://github.com/alexanderalber/transformer-twin-lab): Public source of the pages under `docs/`. Stack is React plus htm and Pico CSS, all vendored locally, no JSX and no bundler.
- [Infinite Alphabets](https://alber.me/infinite-alphabets/): Sister project on the same domain, on automata over infinite alphabets. Unrelated subject, mutually linked.
